We generalise results by Lamberti and Lanza de Cristoforis (2005) concerning the continuity of projections onto eigenspaces of self-adjoint differential operators with compact inverses as the (spatial) domain of the functions is perturbed in R?. Our main case of interest is the Dirichlet Laplacian on a square. We extend their results from bounds from H] to H to bounds from IP to LP, under the assumption that

It is a classical consequence of the Uniform Boundeness Principle that the norm convergence of Fourier series is equivalent to the uniform boundedness of the operator norms of the partial sums (see Grafakos, 2014a, Chap. 4). In dimensions 2 or higher, Fefferman's celebrated theorem (Fefferman, 1971) on the unboundedness of the ball multiplier in IP has as a consequence that we cannot choose the partial sums in any way we want, since convergence is sensitive to the choice of "truncation" for these infinite series. For concreteness, let us fix our dimension d = 2 and consider the lattice Z', which serves to index the Fourier coefficients of a periodic function f : [0, 1] → R. Then there are many ways in which we can group these indices in order to determine the cutoff point for a partial sum of the series

A natural choice would be to truncate by the size of the eigenvalues associated to each exponential (viewed as an eigenfunction of the Laplacian). Up to constants, this would mean fixing N > 0 and summing over all (m, n) with m' + n° < Nº. Geometrically, we are using expanding concentric circles in the lattice to determine the cutoff. As we mentioned earlier, Fefferman's theorem shows that this method never yields IP convergence outside the "trivial" case p = 2. It is a straightforward extension of this result that other "curved" cutoffs, such as ellipses, will also fail to yield convergence (see Grafakos, 2014b, Chap. 5 and its exercises for a discussion). On the other hand, taking squares or rectangles to mark the cutoff does work for all 1 < p < ∞o, as is well-known (see Grafakos, 2014a, Chap. 4). Results by Córdoba (1977) show that other polygonal regions also generate "good" cutoffs within the range 4/3 < p < 4.

One way in which we could explore the issue of convergence in other

planar domains is by perturbation. The idea is to take a planar region I and deform it into another region I. We then study how the eigenfunctions of the Laplacian and the projection operators onto eigenspaces change alongside this change to I. The hope is that, for sufficiently small perturbations we can carry over convergence results on a domain where they are known (e.g. a square, a triangle) to new domains where the problem is still unsolved. The importance of having such I° convergence results for problems in PDE is discussed in Fefferman et al. (2022). They note that a general understanding of IP convergence for eigenfunction expansions is still open, prompting our current efforts.
